name: Public Domain Classics
description: Classical favourites whose composers died long ago, set for the synthesized kit: Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata and Für Elise, Satie's first Gymnopédie, an impression of Debussy's Clair de Lune, Bach's C major Prelude and his Toccata, Pachelbel's Canon with its variations, Ode to Joy in four verses, the Minuet in G with a trio and da capo, and Mozart's Turkish March. These are simplified settings written from memory, not transcriptions. Each is written as a song: one line names the sections, every track says where it plays, repeats and endings are written as in the score, returns are varied, and a tempo map slows each piece into its last bars. They play for two to four minutes and then end. The comments say what was simplified.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Moonlight Sonata (Beethoven)
sketches.description: The first movement in C-sharp minor: the endless triplet figure alone, then the melody of repeated G-sharps over octaves in the bass, a turn to E major, a development through F-sharp minor to the Neapolitan D, a long G-sharp pedal, the opening again with the melody doubled, and a coda that slows into the last chord. A simplified setting, about three minutes.

sketches.name: Für Elise (Beethoven)
sketches.description: The rondo in A minor, in 3/8, with its repeats and first and second endings: the rocking E and D-sharp with the answering arpeggios, the episode that climbs through C major and trills its way back, the stormy section over a hammered A in the bass (louder and doubled the second time), a diminished arpeggio and chromatic fall, the theme once more and a slowing close on A. Simplified, about a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Gymnopédie No. 1 (Satie)
sketches.description: Slow and sorrowful, in 3/4: the bass note and the floating chord alternate between G major seventh and D major seventh, a bare melody drifts in, answers itself and climbs over new harmonies, returns, and after a pause the whole of it comes again, doubled an octave below, before it slows and comes to rest on D. About three and a half minutes.

sketches.name: Clair de Lune (after Debussy)
sketches.description: An impression in the spirit of the piece, not a transcription: a slow 9/8 in D-flat major with rolling arpeggios, a singing line above and the long bass notes underneath. The opening phrase, a second phrase that climbs higher, then a quicker, flowing middle with the arpeggios spread over two octaves, a climax, the opening again and a close that fades and slows. About two and a quarter minutes.

sketches.name: Prelude in C (Bach)
sketches.description: The first prelude of the Well-Tempered Clavier, complete: one broken-chord pattern, five notes rising and then repeated, laid over changing chords. The opening eleven bars, eight more that wander through diminished chords down to C, a descent through F to the long G pedal, and the closing bars over a C pedal, slowing into the final chord. About two minutes.

sketches.name: Canon in D (Pachelbel)
sketches.description: The eight-note ground in the bass goes round once alone, then a plucked arpeggio joins and the violins enter in canon, the second one full ground behind the first, with the viola doubling below from the first variation. The theme gives way to pairs of notes, the falling line in quicker notes and a leaping arpeggio variation; the theme returns in octaves, the ground turns to a cadence and the second violin finishes the round alone. About three and a half minutes.

sketches.name: Ode to Joy (Beethoven)
sketches.description: The melody from the finale of the Ninth Symphony, as four verses after two bars of introduction: plainly in the strings, then with violas doubling and a flute descant, then as the Alla marcia, a third lower in B-flat with bass drum and cymbals, and finally for everyone, with timpani rolls at the end of each phrase, the cymbal and a slowing close. About three and a half minutes.

sketches.name: Minuet in G (Petzold)
sketches.description: The minuet once attributed to Bach, actually by Christian Petzold, in the harpsichord's bright pluck. Both halves with their repeats, then a quieter trio in G minor that turns to B-flat major (a simple setting of its own, not Petzold's companion minuet), and the minuet da capo without repeats, with an octave stop added, slowing into the last bar. About three and a quarter minutes.

sketches.name: Rondo alla Turca (Mozart)
sketches.description: The Turkish March from the Piano Sonata in A, in rondo order with its repeats: the quick turning refrain and its answer, the episode in C major, the bright A major march, a running section in F-sharp minor, the refrain once more and a crashing A major coda that slows to its last chord. A piccolo doubles the march, oom-pah chords sit below and the janissary band plays throughout. Simplified, about two minutes.

sketches.name: Toccata in D minor (Bach)
sketches.description: The organ in a church: the mordent on A and the falling run, doubled an octave below, a diminished chord and the full chord of D minor; the call again an octave lower and a third time lower still; a diminished flourish over the D pedal; the racing toccata figure, a little quicker, over a moving pedal; a cadenza; and a plagal close on D minor that broadens to the end. Simplified, with the dramatic pauses written in, about two and a half minutes.
